data.name: Angular SPA Frontend
data.description: Angular 21 single-page application running in the browser. Serves all Juice Shop UI, stores JWT in localStorage, implements client-side route guards (LoginGuard, AdminGuard), OAuth login callback with derived-password pattern, and WebSocket challenge notifications.

threats.title: [F-001] DOM XSS via Angular Sanitizer Bypass
threats.description:
An attacker sends a victim a link to /#/search?q=<iframe src="javascript:...">. SearchResultComponent reads q from the route, marks it trusted with bypassSecurityTrustHtml and binds it to [innerHTML], so the payload runs in the shop origin and can read the JWT from localStorage.

Impact: Script execution in the victim's session: token theft, account takeover and arbitrary actions as the victim.

Risk: Critical (likelihood High, impact High)
CWE: CWE-79
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
search-result.component.ts:136 reads queryParams.q, line 143 wraps it in bypassSecurityTrustHtml, and search-result.component.html:11 renders searchValue through [innerHTML], skipping Angular's sanitizer.
- frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.ts:143

Abuse-case trace:
- AC-T-001 [fully viable, verification complete] — Account Takeover via XSS + Token Hijacking; matching steps 1 (confirmed)

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-001 (F-001)
threats.mitigation: M-101 — Encode output instead of bypassing the framework sanitizer (priority P1, effort Low) 1. Assign the trimmed query string to searchValue as a plain string and bind it with {{ searchValue }} instead of [innerHTML]; remove the bypassSecurityTrustHtml call. 2. Add a component test that sets q to '' and asserts the #searchValue element contains the literal text and no img element. Verification: Navigate to /#/search?q=%3Cimg%20src%3Dx%20onerror%3Dalert(1)%3E; no dialog appears and #searchValue textContent equals the literal payload. Reference: CWE-79

threats.title: [F-012] Admin test credential embedded in SPA bundle — login.component.ts:62
threats.description:
An anonymous attacker downloads the public JavaScript bundle, reads testingUsername 'testing@juice-sh.op' and testingPassword 'IamU**** (17 chars)' from LoginComponent, and logs in with them. The seeded account with that password carries role admin (data/static/users.yml:271-274), so the attacker obtains an administrator session.

Impact: Administrator access to the shop: all user records, feedback deletion, and every admin-only API, reachable by any visitor.

Risk: High (likelihood High, impact High)
CWE: CWE-798
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
login.component.ts:61-62 hard-code the testing username and password as public component fields shipped in the browser bundle; data/static/users.yml:271-274 seeds that account with the same password and role admin.
- frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:62

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-012 (F-012)
threats.mitigation:
M-110 — Move secrets to a managed secret store (F-012) (priority P2, effort Low)
1. Delete testingUsername and testingPassword from LoginComponent and source any test credential from the e2e test environment instead of application code.
2. Add a build check that greps the production bundle for IamU**** (17 chars) and fails if found.
Verification: npm run build then grep -r IamU**** (17 chars) frontend/dist returns no matches.
Reference: CWE-798

threats.title: [F-013] OAuth-derived predictable password — oauth.component.ts:30
threats.description:
An attacker who knows the email of a user that signed in through Google OAuth computes btoa(reversed email) and submits it with that email to the normal password login, receiving the victim's JWT. The OAuth callback registers every OAuth account with this deterministic password (line 30) and later authenticates with the same derivation (line 46), so the local password is a public function of the identity.

Impact: Full takeover of any OAuth-created account, including its orders, addresses, payment cards and wallet, without access to the Google identity.

Risk: Critical (likelihood High, impact High)
CWE: CWE-1391
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
oauth.component.ts:30 derives the password via btoa(profile.email.split('').reverse().join('')) and passes it to userService.save; line 46 reuses the identical derivation for userService.login, proving the credential is fully predictable from the email.
- frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:30

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-013 (F-013)
threats.mitigation:
M-111 — Remove the derived local password from the OAuth callback (priority P1, effort Medium)
1. Replace the client-side save/login with a server-side OAuth endpoint that validates the Google access token, links the account by verified subject, and issues the session JWT without creating a password-based credential (or creates a random unusable password).
2. Add an API test that registers a user through the OAuth flow and asserts that POST /rest/user/login with btoa(reversed email) returns 401.
Verification: After the change, curl -X POST /rest/user/login -d '{"email":"<oauth user>","password":"<btoa(reversed email)>"}' returns HTTP 401.
Reference: CWE-1391

threats.title: [F-026] Session JWT stored in localStorage — login.component.ts:101
threats.description:
An attacker who achieves script execution through any of the component's sanitizer-bypass sinks (for example search-result.component.ts:143) reads localStorage.token and the JS-readable token cookie and replays them from their own machine. Because the bearer JWT lives in script-accessible storage, a single XSS yields a reusable session valid until token expiry.

Impact: Exfiltrated tokens give full account access, including administrator accounts, beyond the lifetime of the XSS page view.

Risk: High (likelihood High, impact High)
CWE: CWE-922
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
login.component.ts:101 and oauth.component.ts:51 write the JWT to localStorage, login.component.ts:104 also writes it to a JavaScript-set cookie (cannot be HttpOnly), login.component.ts:120 stores totp_tmp_token in localStorage, and request.interceptor.ts:13-16 reads it for every API call.
- frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:101

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-026 (F-026)
threats.mitigation:
M-120 — Store session tokens in HttpOnly, Secure cookies (priority P3, effort High)
1. Have the backend issue the session as an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie and remove localStorage/cookieService token writes in login, oauth and two-factor components; drop the Authorization header from RequestInterceptor.
2. Add an e2e test that logs in and asserts localStorage.getItem('token') is null and document.cookie does not contain token.
Verification: After login in Cypress, cy.window().its('localStorage.token').should('not.exist') and document.cookie lacks a token entry.
Reference: CWE-922

threats.title: [F-033] OAuth implicit flow without state — oauth.component.ts:28
threats.description:
An attacker obtains a Google access token for an attacker-controlled account and sends the victim a link to /#access_token=<attacker token>. The OAuth component accepts any access_token from the URL fragment without a state value, so the victim is silently logged into the attacker's shop account and may store addresses or payment cards there.

Impact: Login CSRF: the victim acts inside an attacker-owned account, so entered addresses, cards and order data become visible to the attacker.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-352
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
login.component.ts:148 starts the implicit flow (response_type=token) without a state parameter; oauth.component.ts:28 passes parseRedirectUrlParams().access_token straight to oauthLogin and then logs in, with no state or nonce comparison anywhere in the callback.
- frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:28

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-033 (F-033)
threats.mitigation:
M-125 — Add anti-CSRF protection to state-changing requests (priority P3, effort Medium)
1. Switch to authorization code flow with PKCE, generate a random state stored in sessionStorage in googleLogin(), and reject the callback in OAuthComponent when the returned state is missing or differs.
2. Add a frontend unit test that navigates to the callback with a valid-looking access_token but no state and asserts oauthLogin is never called.
Verification: Opening /#access_token=abc without a matching state leaves the user logged out and no /rest/user/whoami-authenticated call succeeds.
Reference: RFC 9700

threats.title: [F-065] Client-side-only admin route guard — app.guard.ts:54
threats.description:
An authenticated customer bypasses AdminGuard by navigating directly to /#/administration after editing the unverified JWT payload in localStorage, or simply calls the APIs the admin view uses. The guard decodes the token with jwtDecode without signature verification, and the backing GET /api/Users route requires only authentication (server.ts:363), so the customer sees every user record shown in the admin panel.

Impact: Non-admin users read the full user list (emails, roles, login state) presented by the admin panel.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-602
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
app.guard.ts:38 decodes the token client-side without verification and line 54 grants the route when payload.data.role equals admin; app.routing.ts:81 protects /administration solely with this guard, while server.ts:363 applies only isAuthorized() to GET /api/Users.
- frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:54

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-065 (F-065)
threats.mitigation:
M-141 — Enforce authorization on the server (F-065) (priority P3, effort Medium)
1. Treat AdminGuard as UX only and add a server-side admin-role check (verified JWT role) on GET /api/Users and feedback management routes consumed by AdministrationComponent.
2. Add API tests asserting a customer token receives 403 from GET /api/Users while an admin token receives 200.
Verification: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <customer JWT>' /api/Users returns HTTP 403.
Reference: CWE-602

data.name: Express API Server
data.description: Node.js 24 Express application server that registers all REST API routes and middleware. Implements business logic for products, basket, orders, feedback, file uploads, LLM chat, and admin/management endpoints. Acts as trust boundary between browser clients and internal data stores.

threats.title: [F-003] SQL injection in product search — routes/search.ts:23
threats.description:
An anonymous attacker sends GET /rest/products/search?q=')) UNION SELECT id,email,password,... FROM Users--; the q value is interpolated into a raw sequelize.query() string, so the attacker rewrites the query and receives every user's email and password hash in the JSON response.

Impact: Unauthenticated read of the whole SQLite database, including user credentials (declared sensitive asset) and card data.

Risk: Critical (likelihood High, impact Critical)
CWE: CWE-89
CVSS v4: 8.7 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N)
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
req.query.q (routes/search.ts:21) is concatenated into the SQL text at routes/search.ts:23 with only a 200-character length cap; the route has no authentication (server.ts:602).
- routes/search.ts:23

threats.description:
A signed-in attacker puts another user's ID into the owner field of the request (req.body.UserId and the like); the query trusts it instead of the session identity, so the attacker reads or changes every other user's records — horizontal privilege escalation across all accounts.

Risk: Critical (likelihood Critical, impact Critical)
CWE: CWE-639
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: source-scan

Evidence:
- routes/address.ts:11

threats.mitigation:

threats.title: [F-005] SQL injection authentication bypass — routes/login.ts:34
threats.description:
An anonymous attacker posts to /rest/user/login with email admin@juice-sh.op'-- and any password; the email is interpolated into the raw SELECT, the comment removes the password predicate, and the server issues a signed session token for the administrator.

Impact: Unauthenticated login as any user including admin, exposing all credentials, addresses and payment cards (declared sensitive assets).

Risk: Critical (likelihood High, impact Critical)
CWE: CWE-89
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
req.body.email is concatenated into sequelize.query() at routes/login.ts:34; only the password is hashed, and afterLogin() signs a token for whatever row returns (lines 21-26).
- routes/login.ts:34

Trust boundary crossings:
- tb-6 auth → database (internal): The auth-to-SQLite crossing assumes parameterized binding, but the login query interpolates the submitted email into SQL text.

updateUserProfile stores req.body.username at routes/updateUserProfile.ts:38; getUserProfile matches /#{(.*)}/ and calls eval(code) at routes/userProfile.ts:61. Active when usernameXssChallenge is enabled.

threats.title: [F-007] Hardcoded JWT signing key — lib/insecurity.ts:21
threats.description:
An anonymous attacker copies the RSA private key embedded at lib/insecurity.ts:21, signs a JWT whose data claims id 1 and role admin, and sends it as a Bearer token; security.isAuthorized() and updateAuthenticatedUsers() verify it against the matching public key and register it, so the attacker acts as any user including the administrator.

Impact: Complete authentication bypass: the attacker impersonates any customer or admin and reaches their stored credentials, addresses, and payment cards (declared sensitive assets).

Risk: High (likelihood High, impact Critical)
CWE: CWE-321
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: configuration-defect

Evidence:
The private key used by security.authorize() to sign every session token is a string literal in source, so any reader can mint tokens that pass isAuthorized() at lib/insecurity.ts:52.
- lib/insecurity.ts:21

applied fields: sensitive assets; source: docs/security/business-context.md; sha256: 1df5d78a86a217e38319c02829c25ca9b1ec6a09b2361d3b607a6b7f651b5851

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-007 (F-007)
threats.mitigation:
M-106 — Load JWT signing key from secret store (priority P2, effort Medium)
1. Remove the privateKey literal from lib/insecurity.ts and load a per-deployment RSA key from an external secret store at startup, failing closed when absent.
2. Rotate the key and invalidate every token signed with the old key.
3. Add a test that signs a token with the old committed key and asserts isAuthorized() rejects it with 401.
Verification: Sign a JWT with the old committed key and call GET /rest/basket/1; expect HTTP 401.
Reference: CWE-321

threats.title: [F-009] Insecure JWT Verification
threats.description:
An anonymous attacker sends a JWT whose header names alg none or HS256 keyed with the published jwt.pub; isAuthorized() passes the token to express-jwt 0.1.3 / jsonwebtoken 0.4.0 without an algorithms allowlist, so the header-selected algorithm is honoured and the forged identity is accepted.

Impact: Any caller can forge tokens for arbitrary users and roles, bypassing authentication on every isAuthorized()-protected route.

Risk: High (likelihood Medium, impact High)
CWE: CWE-347
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
isAuthorized() configures expressJwt with only the public key at lib/insecurity.ts:52 and package.json pins express-jwt 0.1.3 and jsonwebtoken 0.4.0, versions that honour the token-supplied alg header.
- lib/insecurity.ts:52

- AC-T-003 [inconclusive, verification complete] — Privilege Escalation to Admin via JWT Algorithm Confusion; matching steps 1 (confirmed)

2. Add negative tests sending alg none and HS256-with-public-key tokens to an isAuthorized() route.
Verification: Send an alg:none token and an HS256 token keyed with jwt.pub to GET /rest/2fa/status; both must return 401.

resetPassword() accepts email plus security answer as the only proof at routes/resetPassword.ts:41 and updates the password at line 44; the limiter key derives from forwarded headers at server.ts:342-346.
- routes/resetPassword.ts:41

threats.title: [F-042] Client-asserted challenge verification trusted — registerWebsocketEvents.ts:41
threats.description:
An attacker emits verifyLocalXssChallenge with the literal string '<iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)">' (or verifySvgInjectionChallenge with a matching path string, or verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge with any two-element array) without ever executing the exploit, and the server calls challengeUtils.solve(), which sets challenge.solved=true and persists it via challenge.save().

Impact: Challenge completion state, the CTF flag notification and the optional SOLUTIONS_WEBHOOK report (challengeUtils.ts:39-40) can be produced without performing the exploit, so the training instance's progress and scoreboard records lose integrity.

Risk: Medium (likelihood High, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-602
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
Line 41 decides solved state solely by utils.contains on the client-sent data; lines 46 and 50 do the same for SVG injection and close-notifications; challengeUtils.ts:30-31 then persists solved=true.
- lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:41

Trust boundary crossings:
- tb-1 external → realtime-channel (internet-facing): Handler processes a client-asserted verification event and mutates challenge state without authorizing the principal or validating server-observed evidence.

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-042 (F-042)
threats.mitigation:
M-130 — Enforce authorization on the server (F-042) (priority P3, effort Medium)
1. Replace the client-reported verify* handlers with server-observed evidence (e.g. detect the XSS payload in the server-side search or render request) or bind each verification to a one-time server-issued nonce tied to the authenticated session.
2. Add an API test that emits verifyLocalXssChallenge with the payload string from a fresh socket and asserts the challenge remains unsolved.
Verification: Emit verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge with [1,2] from a raw socket.io-client; expect GET /api/Challenges to still show closeNotificationsChallenge solved=false.
Reference: CWE-602

threats.title: [F-052] CTF flags pushed to every unauthenticated socket — registerWebsocketEvents.ts:30
threats.description:
An anonymous attacker connects to the Socket.IO endpoint and immediately receives every queued 'challenge solved' notification, each carrying the CTF flag from utils.ctfFlag(challenge.name), and keeps receiving new flags via the global io.emit broadcast in challengeUtils.ts:75.

Impact: On a shared instance, any network client harvests CTF flags for challenges solved by others and can submit them to the CTF scoreboard, undermining the training event's scoring integrity.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-200
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
Line 30 replays the whole notifications array to each new socket; challengeUtils.ts:52 and 66 put the computed flag into each notification and line 75 broadcasts it to all connected sockets.
- lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:30

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-052 (F-052)
threats.mitigation:
M-135 — Stop exposing internal information to clients (priority P3, effort Medium)
1. After adding handshake authentication, join each socket to a per-user or per-instance-owner room and replace io.emit in challengeUtils.ts:75 and the replay loop at line 29-31 with emits to that room only; omit the flag field unless CTF mode requires it for that owner.
2. Add an API test that connects an unauthenticated socket and asserts no 'challenge solved' event containing a flag is received.
Verification: Solve a challenge, then connect a raw socket.io-client without credentials; expect zero 'challenge solved' events.
Reference: CWE-200

threats.title: [F-058] Unanchored backtracking regex on socket payload — registerWebsocketEvents.ts:46
threats.description:
While the SVG injection challenge is unsolved, an anonymous attacker repeatedly emits verifySvgInjectionChallenge with a near-1 MB string of non-matching characters; the unanchored pattern /.*\.\.\/\.\.\/\.\.[\w/-]*?\/redirect.../ is retried from every start offset with a greedy .* backtrack, giving quadratic work on the single Node.js event loop.

Impact: Each event can block the event loop shared with the api-backend HTTP server, stalling the whole training instance for all users.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-1333
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
Line 46 runs data?.match() with a leading unanchored .* on unvalidated attacker data; the Server at line 20 sets no maxHttpBufferSize override and no payload length check precedes the match.
- lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:46

Trust boundary crossings:
- tb-1 external → realtime-channel (internet-facing): Event payload reaches an expensive regex without type or length validation, breaking the tb-1 validation leg.

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-058 (F-058)
threats.mitigation:
M-138 — Bound payload and anchor regex (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Reject non-string or over-length data (e.g. > 2048 chars) before matching, and rewrite the pattern without the leading .* (use RegExp.test on /\.\.\/\.\.\/\.\.[\w/-]*?\/redirect\?to=https?:\/\/cataas\.com\/cat/).
2. Add a server unit test that passes a 1 MB non-matching string to the handler and asserts it returns within 50 ms.
Verification: Emit verifySvgInjectionChallenge with 'a'.repeat(1000000) and measure event-loop lag; expect under 50 ms.
Reference: CWE-1333

threats.title: [F-034] Open redirect — routes/redirect.ts:19
threats.description:
An attacker sends a victim a shop link /redirect?to=<attacker URL> that embeds an allowlisted URL as a substring; the server passes isRedirectAllowed and issues a 302 to the attacker site, which then impersonates the shop for phishing.

Impact: Victims are sent from a trusted shop URL to an attacker-controlled origin, enabling credential phishing and malware delivery under the shop's reputation.

Risk: Medium (likelihood High, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-601
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
redirect.ts:15 reads query.to, line 16 gates it with security.isRedirectAllowed, and line 19 calls res.redirect(toUrl). Lines 18 and 27-32 award the redirect challenge when a URL passes isRedirectAllowed but does not start with any allowlist entry, proving the gate accepts URLs that are not prefix-matched to an allowlisted destination.
- routes/redirect.ts:19

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-034 (F-034)
threats.mitigation:
M-126 — Validate redirect targets against an allowlist (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Parse query.to with new URL(), reject non-https schemes, and require the full URL (or origin plus path) to equal an allowlist entry instead of a substring/includes test.
2. Add API tests asserting /redirect?to=https://evil.example/?x=<allowlisted URL> returns 406 and an exact allowlisted URL still returns 302.
Verification: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost:3000/redirect?to=https://evil.example/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop' returns 406.
Reference: CWE-601

threats.title: [F-053] Hardcoded BIP39 wallet mnemonic — routes/checkKeys.ts:10
threats.description:
An attacker reads the 12-word mnemonic literal from the source (or shipped server bundle), derives the HD wallet with HDNodeWallet.fromPhrase, and obtains the private key that both controls the Ethereum wallet and unlocks the NFT challenge endpoint.

Impact: Anyone with source access controls the wallet's private key and any assets on it; the architecture context assumes testnet-only funds, which bounds but does not remove the exposure.

Risk: Medium (likelihood High, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-798
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
checkKeys.ts:10 embeds the mnemonic as a string literal; line 11 derives the wallet and line 12 its privateKey, which line 16-18 compares against req.body.privateKey as the unlock secret.
- routes/checkKeys.ts:10

- AC-T-005 [fully viable, verification complete] — Authentication Bypass via Exposed Secret Material; matching steps 1 (confirmed)

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-053 (F-053)
threats.mitigation:
M-136 — Move secrets to a managed secret store (F-053) (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Remove the literal, load the mnemonic or only the expected address from a secret store or environment variable at startup, and fail closed when it is absent; rotate the exposed wallet.
2. Add a secret-scanning check (e.g. gitleaks rule for BIP39 phrases) to CI and a test that startup fails without the configured secret.
Verification: grep -rnE "'([a-z]+ ){11}[a-z]+'" routes/ returns no hits.

threats.title: [F-059] Unbounded walletsConnected growth from request body — routes/web3Wallet.ts:16
threats.description:
An attacker repeatedly posts unique or large walletAddress values to the contract exploit listener endpoint; each value is added to the module-level walletsConnected Set, which is only pruned when a matching on-chain ContractExploited event arrives, so process memory grows until the Node.js server degrades or crashes.

Impact: Memory exhaustion of the shared server process takes down the entire shop instance for all users.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-770
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
web3Wallet.ts:15 reads req.body.walletAddress without type or length validation and line 16 adds it to the global Set declared at line 10; the only removal is line 28 on a matching exploit event. Whether the route is authenticated is decided in router code outside this component and was not inspected.
- routes/web3Wallet.ts:16

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-059 (F-059)
threats.mitigation:
M-085 — Validate and bound walletsConnected entries in routes/web3Wallet.ts (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Accept walletAddress only when ethers.isAddress() is true, normalise with getAddress(), and cap the Set size (or use an LRU with TTL) before adding.
2. Add a server test posting a non-address and an oversized string, asserting 400 and that the Set size does not grow.
Verification: Send 1000 POST requests with unique random non-address strings as walletAddress to the wallet endpoint; assert each returns 400 and that the process RSS measured before and after stays within 5 MB, confirming invalid entries are rejected and the Set remains bounded.
Reference: CWE-770

data.name: CI/CD Pipeline

threats.title: [F-020] Lockfile-free npm install into published image
threats.description:
An attacker who publishes a malicious version of any direct or transitive dependency inside a declared semver range gets it resolved by `npm install --omit=dev` in the Docker build, because `.npmrc` sets `package-lock=false` and no lockfile exists; its install scripts run during the build and the code ships in the image pushed to Docker Hub.

Impact: Malicious code executes at build time and persists in the published image, matching the declared harm that a compromised pipeline injects code into Docker images used by training deployments worldwide.

Risk: High (likelihood Medium, impact High)
CWE: CWE-829
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: stride

Evidence:
Dockerfile:5 runs `npm install --omit=dev` (lifecycle scripts enabled); .npmrc:1 sets `package-lock=false`; no package-lock.json exists and .gitignore:10 ignores it; ci.yml:51/71/110/147/203/238/292 also use `npm install`.
- Dockerfile:5

threats.description:
Missing Workflow Permissions Block: Without an explicit permissions block at workflow or job level, the job inherits the repository default (commonly write-all) for GITHUB_TOKEN — any compromised step can push code, create releases, or approve PRs.

Risk: Medium (likelihood Medium, impact Medium)
CWE: CWE-732
Evidence tier: confirmed-exploitable
Source: config-scan

Evidence:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:25

Business-context trace:
applied fields: impact if compromised, security obligations; source: docs/security/business-context.md; sha256: 1df5d78a86a217e38319c02829c25ca9b1ec6a09b2361d3b607a6b7f651b5851

Full finding: threat-model.md#f-064 (F-064)
threats.mitigation:
M-100 — Apply least-privilege permissions (priority P3, effort Low)
1. Add `permissions: { contents: read }` at workflow root; elevate per-job only where needed
2. Add a regression test (or CI check) that fails on the vulnerable pattern and passes once the fix is in place.
Verification: Re-run the IAC-010 scanner check; it reports no match at .github/workflows/ci.yml:25, and the regression test passes.

data.description: OpenAI-compatible LLM inference endpoint (or local Ollama) used by the /rest/chat route for AI-SDK streaming chat completions. Base URL is read from application config.

data.name: Google OAuth
data.description: Google accounts OAuth 2.0 authorization server used by the Angular frontend for browser-only login. No server-side OAuth code path exists; the frontend derives a password from the returned email and calls the standard login endpoint.
